steps.tx: **Amyloidosis** encompasses protein-folding disorders wherein soluble precursor proteins aggregate into insoluble, unbranched **7.5 to 10 nanometre cross-beta-sheet fibrils**. Extracellular deposition in interstitial tissue progressively disrupts normal tissue architecture and impairs vital organ function.
steps.say: Amyloidosis is a protein-misfolding disorder forming unbranched cross-beta-sheet fibrils. Extracellular deposition causes progressive organ dysfunction.

vis.alt: Amyloid fibril formation and extracellular deposition pathways
vis.caption: Misfolded precursor proteins aggregate into rigid cross-beta fibrils that deposit extracellularly. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Definitive histopathologic diagnosis requires tissue biopsy showing pathognomonic **apple-green birefringence** under cross-polarized light microscopy following **Congo red staining**. Initial screening relies on abdominal subcutaneous fat pad aspiration with **70 to 80 percent sensitivity**, followed by labial salivary gland or direct organ biopsy.
steps.say: Diagnosis requires Congo red staining demonstrating apple-green birefringence under polarized light. Abdominal fat pad aspiration provides 70 to 80 percent screening sensitivity.

nodes.label: Abdominal subcutaneous fat pad aspirate or organ biopsy
Congo red histochemical staining of tissue sections
Pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under cross-polarized microscopy

steps.tx: **AL amyloidosis** is caused by a clonal plasma cell dyscrasia producing misfolded monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains, predominantly **lambda light chains in 75 percent**. Hallmark clinical signs include nephrotic syndrome, restrictive cardiomyopathy with low ECG voltages, pathognomonic **macroglossia in 15 percent**, and periorbital ecchymoses or **raccoon eyes**.
steps.say: AL amyloidosis is caused by clonal plasma cell light chains, mostly lambda. Hallmarks include nephrotic syndrome, restrictive cardiomyopathy, macroglossia, and raccoon eyes.

vis.alt: Clinical hallmarks of AL amyloidosis: macroglossia, purpura, and nephrotic syndrome
vis.caption: AL amyloidosis features light-chain deposition causing macroglossia and purpura. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **AA amyloidosis** is reactive to sustained, chronic systemic inflammation such as long-standing rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, familial Mediterranean fever, or chronic bronchiectasis. Cytokines IL-6 and IL-1 stimulate hepatic overproduction of acute-phase **serum amyloid A**, whose cleavage fragments deposit predominantly in renal glomeruli causing heavy **nephrotic proteinuria**.
steps.say: AA amyloidosis develops from chronic inflammation like rheumatoid arthritis or FMF. Hepatic serum amyloid A deposits in kidneys, producing heavy proteinuria.

rows: Chronic IL-6 driving hepatic SAA synthesis
Progressive renal failure; prevented by colchicine

steps.tx: **Transthyretin amyloidosis** or ATTR arises from misfolded transthyretin. It occurs as **wild-type ATTRwt**, formerly senile amyloidosis, affecting elderly men with restrictive cardiomyopathy and bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, or as hereditary mutant **variant ATTRv**, caused by mutations such as **Val122Ile** or **Val30Met** causing familial amyloid polyneuropathy and cardiomyopathy.
steps.say: Transthyretin amyloidosis occurs as wild-type in elderly men or as hereditary mutant variants. Mutations like Val30Met produce familial polyneuropathy and cardiomyopathy.

left.title: Wild-type ATTR (ATTRwt)
points: Carpal tunnel syndrome precedes heart failure

right.title: Variant hereditary ATTR (ATTRv)
points: Earlier clinical onset in middle age

steps.tx: Cardiac amyloidosis characteristically shows concentric biventricular wall thickening with small ventricular cavities and severe diastolic dysfunction. A classic diagnostic paradox is **low QRS voltage on ECG despite thickened ventricular myocardium on echocardiography**, alongside **apical sparing** of longitudinal strain on echocardiographic speckle tracking.
steps.say: Cardiac amyloidosis exhibits low ECG voltages despite marked ventricular thickening on echocardiogram. Speckle tracking demonstrates a classic apical sparing pattern.

nodes.label: Amyloid fibril infiltration of ventricular myocardium
Concentric ventricular thickening with low QRS voltages on ECG
Preserved apical strain with impaired basal strain (apical sparing)

steps.tx: Nuclear bone scintigraphy with **technetium-99m pyrophosphate** or 99mTc-PYP enables non-biopsy diagnosis of ATTR cardiac amyloidosis. Intense myocardial tracer uptake reaching **Perugini grade 2 or 3**, when combined with negative serum and urine immunofixation and normal serum free light chain ratios, confirms ATTR cardiomyopathy without endomyocardial biopsy.
steps.say: Technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy showing grade 2 or 3 uptake confirms ATTR cardiac amyloidosis non-invasively, provided monoclonal light chains are excluded.

rows: Myocardial uptake less than rib uptake
Myocardial uptake equal to or greater than rib uptake
Diagnostic of ATTR cardiomyopathy if light chains negative

steps.tx: Modern therapy directly targets precursor protein production. AL amyloidosis is treated with anti-plasma cell regimens combining **daratumumab, bortezomib, cyclophosphamide, and dexamethasone**. In ATTR amyloidosis, the oral kinetic tetramer stabilizer **tafamidis at 61 mg daily** or gene-silencing siRNA **patisiran** halts neurologic and cardiac disease progression.
steps.say: AL amyloidosis is treated with daratumumab, bortezomib, and dexamethasone. ATTR cardiomyopathy responds to tafamidis or gene-silencing agents like patisiran.

left.title: AL amyloidosis therapy
points: Followed by autologous stem cell transplantation

right.title: ATTR amyloidosis therapy
points: Tafamidis 61 mg daily stabilizes TTR tetramers
Patisiran or vutrisiran silences hepatic TTR synthesis
